newsitem.title: Bangladesh: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 29.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The visiting World Bank vice president Meiko Nishimizu said on Tuesday that the bank would continue its support to Bangladesh's infrastructural development.
U.S. Assistant Secretary of State Robin Raphel said in Dhaka on Tueaday that Washington supported the concept of four-nation sub-regional bloc in South Asia.
The British Overseas Trade Board Chairman Martin Laing said on Tuesday three more trade delegations from Britain would be visiting Bangladesh this year to interact with Bangladeshi businessmen.
Cargo handling at the Mongla Port came to a halt on Tuesday after part time workers went on strike for an indefinite period to press their 15-point demands.
Energy Minister Noor uddin Khan told parliament on Tuesday that his ministry had permitted a private firm, Rural Power Company Ltd, to raise capital from the share market.
The High Court on Tuesday held the Indemnity (Repeal) Act, 1996, passed by a simple majority in the parliament, as a valid law.
The European Commission has assured Bangladesh of considering its request for derogation of a law relating to Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) for knit garments.
A three-member Japanese business delegation led by Kazuyoshi Ariga, vice president of All Japan Federation of Commerce and Industry Associations, started on Tuesday its week-long visit to Bangladesh.
